A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowR and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing experiments and supplementary material can be matched reliably despite renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original FlowR reconstruction results on DL3DV140, ScanNet++, Nerfbusters, and Mip-NeRF 360, together with component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a memory-versus-performance comparison in Appendix A.2, Table 7.

M1.justification: The reconstruction pipeline, conditional flow formulation, multi-view transformer, losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Expanded architecture specifications and explanations document the existing method rather than establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training still uses DL3DV10K and ScanNet++; evaluation retains DL3DV140, ScanNet++, Nerfbusters, and Mip-NeRF 360. The new view-count comparison uses existing coverage rather than introducing a dataset or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets, including InstantSplat, ViewCrafter, GANeRF, and Nerfbusters. The Mip-NeRF 360 comparison retains ZipNeRF, ZeroNVS, ReconFusion, and CAT3D in v1 Table 8 and v2 Table 9; newly cited works are not added baselines.

E3.justification: New Table 7 compares processing 72 versus 12 views per forward pass on DL3DV140 at 512-pixel width and reports GPU memory alongside image-quality metrics. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, resolutions, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a small sensitivity analysis testing whether fewer jointly processed views reduce memory requirements while maintaining reconstruction quality. The earlier reconstruction, source-distribution, and loss/reinitialization ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these results. The new memory comparison does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports 42.3 GB for 72 views and 17.0 GB for 12 views, with new 12-view PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS results of 24.29/0.801/0.175; the 72-view quality values repeat Table 5. Appendix A.1 also adds an initial-rendering PSNR range from 5 to over 30. All eight original result tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Equation 2 explicitly distinguishes evaluated spherical-harmonic color from its parameters, clarifying the view-dependent color already used in v1. The underlying mathematics, flow-matching derivations, and assumptions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the explicit claim to be the first to formulate the problem through flow matching and instead emphasizes the hypothesis favoring direct conditional transport over noise-to-data generation. The central reconstruction contributions and sparse/dense performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains the separate generated-view loss through possible imperfections such as VAE compression artifacts. Appendix A.2 adds the static-scene limitation and requirements for extending to dynamic objects, and interprets the memory comparison as supporting use on memory-constrained GPUs.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies 24 DiT blocks, 24 attention heads of dimension 64, and feedforward width 1536, and reports concrete memory requirements. These additions improve documentation of the existing architecture; training schedules and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to denoising diffusion probabilistic models, SP2360, and latent diffusion, while revising the introductory positioning against noise-to-data generation. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are partially rewritten, several method explanations are clarified, and appendix architecture and limitations paragraphs are expanded. An author name is shortened, but the overall section organization and most experimental prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the memory comparison table, updates Figure 1's example images and notation, and embeds higher-resolution images in Figures 3–4. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and surrounding text reflows, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added architecture specifications improve reproducibility, while Table 7 supplies useful evidence about memory requirements and image quality. The explicit static-scene limitation also clarifies applicability. These are supported but limited gains: the core method and original benchmark comparisons remain unchanged.
